title: OtaconsKeep Continuity Model
honesty: The Continuity Model (CM-01...CM-25) is the design theory for behavioral continuity. Runtime modules implement a subset today (emotional continuity + Formula 5). Worked traces labeled MOCK are synthetic. This page does not claim human consciousness, it claims measurable, bounded state dynamics.
manual_note: The OtaconsKeep continuity model is derived from a practical blend of trait psychology, appraisal-based emotion logic, memory relevance scoring, relationship reinforcement, and state regulation principles. It does not claim to reproduce human consciousness. Instead, it uses mathematically simple but psychologically grounded mechanisms to simulate continuity, emotional carryover, social weighting, and context-sensitive behavior over time. The original equations define the behavioral engine. Stability-layer equations (caps, identity anchor, output evaluation) bound per-cycle change, preserve identity, limit memory dominance, and evaluate output quality.
diluted_version: It feels different depending on what happened
Then it decides what to say or do

rationale.title: Why this emulates continuity (not consciousness)
body: Human-like persistence is approximated by carrying a state vector, relationship graph, and memory scores across turns, the opposite of stateless autocomplete.
Multiplication models interaction (pain × trauma relevance); summation models accumulation (many events in one cycle).
Decay and baselines model regulation / homeostasis so affect does not spiral forever.
Bounded noise prevents robotic sameness without becoming chaos.
Identity anchor (β_i ≥ β_min) keeps character from dissolving under adaptation.

Markov stage labels and OR goal programs add probabilistic and decision-theoretic structure on top of the continuous engine, useful for analysis, planning, and V&V, without replacing the continuous math.

core_logic_justification.multiplication: Used when one factor should amplify or dampen another (event hurt × trauma; praise × trust; trait × trigger).
core_logic_justification.summation: Used when multiple inputs all contribute (many events on mood; many social signals; competing memories).
core_logic_justification.decay: Pulls values toward baseline so the system recovers and stays long-run stable.
core_logic_justification.bounded_noise: Small η prevents identical replies while remaining coherent.

chapters.title: Trait Weight Model
katex: W_t = B_D \cdot S_t \cdot C_t \cdot P_t \cdot K_t \cdot (1+\varepsilon_t)
chapters.meaning: Converts a written dossier trait into a usable numeric weight.
chapters.why_this_logic: Multiplicative model: traits do not stack flatly, they amplify or weaken each other by category, certainty, personality, and context. Example: PTSD weighs more than coffee dependence; inferred traits weigh less than canonical; same trait matters differently across personalities.
chapters.why_these_variables: B_D = category seriousness; S_t = not all trauma/habits equal; C_t = known vs guessed; P_t = personality changes expression; K_t = context; ε_t = avoid robotic sameness.
chapters.simple_explanation: How strong is this trait for this agent?

simplified.headline: How strong is this trait for this agent?
simplified.plain_equation: In words: Converts a written dossier trait into a usable numeric weight.
simplified.how_it_touches_agents: When an agent is loaded, dossier traits are scored into weights. A high weight means that trait can pull harder on later behavior if it becomes active.
simplified.how_it_works: Multiplicative model: traits do not stack flatly, they amplify or weaken each other by category, certainty, personality, and context. Example: PTSD weighs more than coffee dependence; inferred traits weigh less than canonical; same trait matters differently across personalities.
simplified.why_it_works: Multiplication was chosen because seriousness, confidence, personality, and context should scale each other rather than add as equals.
simplified.how_put_together: This is the entry gate from written character sheets into numbers the rest of the stack can use.
simplified.connects_to: Upstream inputs become numbers; downstream equations consume those numbers during the agent turn.

chapters.title: Active Trait Influence Model
chapters.meaning: Decides whether a trait matters right now.
chapters.why_this_logic: A strong trait should not always dominate. It becomes active when something triggers it, the right person is involved, and memory makes it relevant.
chapters.why_these_variables: G = triggers activate latent traits; R = traits hit differently by who is involved; M = recent/emotional memories amplify relevance.
chapters.simple_explanation: Does this trait matter in this moment?

simplified.headline: Does this trait matter in this moment?
simplified.plain_equation: In words: Decides whether a trait matters right now.
variables_explained: A_t(t) is active influence at time t.
simplified.how_it_touches_agents: On each turn, stored weights are multiplied by trigger match, relationship relevance, and memory recency. Only then does a trait push the agent.
simplified.how_it_works: A strong trait should not always dominate. It becomes active when something triggers it, the right person is involved, and memory makes it relevant.
simplified.why_it_works: A strong PTSD trait stays quiet until a trigger, the right person, and a relevant memory line up. That matches how latent traits behave in people.
simplified.how_put_together: Active influence feeds conflict resolution and output assembly later in the stack.
simplified.connects_to: Upstream inputs become numbers; downstream equations consume those numbers during the agent turn.

chapters.title: Event Impact on State
chapters.meaning: Calculates how events change an internal state variable (mood, stress, confidence, ...).

variables.def: total change in state X at time t
set of events active at time t
base effect of event e on state X

chapters.why_this_logic: Summation over events (many things can affect someone at once). Multiplication inside each event (raw effect filtered by personality, relationships, history).
chapters.why_these_variables: E = event strength; Q = personalities react differently; L = who caused it matters; H = past pain amplifies impact.
chapters.simple_explanation: How much did what just happened affect me?

simplified.headline: How much did what just happened affect me?
simplified.plain_equation: In words: Calculates how events change an internal state variable (mood, stress, confidence, ...).
variables_explained: \Delta X(t) is total change in state X at time t.
\mathcal{E}_t is set of events active at time t.
E_{e,x} is base effect of event e on state X.
simplified.how_it_touches_agents: Incoming events (praise, rejection, comparison, tool failure) become a change to mood or stress. Personality, who caused it, and past pain scale the hit.
simplified.how_it_works: Summation over events (many things can affect someone at once). Multiplication inside each event (raw effect filtered by personality, relationships, history).
simplified.why_it_works: Summing events lets several things land in one cycle. Multiplying inside each event keeps the raw hit honest to who and what.
simplified.how_put_together: These deltas are the fuel for the state update equation that follows.
simplified.connects_to: Upstream inputs become numbers; downstream equations consume those numbers during the agent turn.

chapters.title: State Update Model
chapters.meaning: Updates an internal state over time with event drive, noise, decay-to-baseline, and bounds.
chapters.why_this_logic: Dynamic system: events move state; noise prevents robotic sameness; decay pulls toward baseline; clamp prevents runaway.
chapters.why_these_variables: η = humans are not perfectly deterministic; λ = emotions settle; X* = natural baseline.
chapters.simple_explanation: How do I feel now after everything that happened?

simplified.headline: How do I feel now after everything that happened?
simplified.plain_equation: In words: Updates an internal state over time with event drive, noise, decay-to-baseline, and bounds.
simplified.how_it_touches_agents: After events, the agent’s internal numbers move: add the capped event change, add a little noise, then decay toward the agent’s baseline, then clamp.
simplified.how_it_works: Dynamic system: events move state; noise prevents robotic sameness; decay pulls toward baseline; clamp prevents runaway.
simplified.why_it_works: Without decay and clamps, jealousy or trust would walk off to infinity. Noise stops identical robotic replies.
simplified.how_put_together: This is the heartbeat of continuous affect between Codec turns.
simplified.connects_to: Upstream inputs become numbers; downstream equations consume those numbers during the agent turn.

chapters.title: Relationship Update Model
chapters.meaning: Updates a relationship dimension toward target j (trust, admiration, resentment, ...).
chapters.why_this_logic: Relationships change gradually through repeated events with inertia, avoid unrealistic instant swings.
chapters.why_these_variables: ΔY = events strengthen/weaken bonds; μ = sticky relationships; Y* = natural trust bias.
chapters.simple_explanation: Do I trust or resent this person more now?

simplified.headline: Do I trust or resent this person more now?
simplified.plain_equation: In words: Updates a relationship dimension toward target j (trust, admiration, resentment, ...).
variables_explained: Y_{j,t} is relationship value toward j.
Y_j^\star is baseline tendency toward that target.
simplified.how_it_touches_agents: Directed scores toward another agent or the user (trust, resentment, admiration) update the same way: events move them, inertia slows resets, baselines matter.
simplified.how_it_works: Relationships change gradually through repeated events with inertia, avoid unrealistic instant swings.
simplified.why_it_works: Directed edges matter because A can trust B while B remains wary of A. That matches the About page relationship claim.
simplified.how_put_together: Relationship scores later change how hard social signals and events land.
simplified.connects_to: Upstream inputs become numbers; downstream equations consume those numbers during the agent turn.

chapters.why_this_logic: Not all social signals matter equally, tone, public/private, source, and sensitivity interact.
chapters.why_these_variables: V = tone; U = public hits harder; L = some people matter more; Z = absorption differs by agent.
chapters.simple_explanation: How much did that post or message affect me?

simplified.why_it_works: Public insults from someone close should hit harder than private noise from a stranger. The product of those factors encodes that.

chapters.title: Emotional Residue Model
chapters.meaning: Models leftover emotional carryover from earlier events.
chapters.why_this_logic: People do not reset after each event, some feeling remains and carries forward.
chapters.why_these_variables: ρ = traces persist; ω = events leave different residue amounts.
chapters.simple_explanation: Am I still carrying the feeling from earlier?

simplified.headline: Am I still carrying the feeling from earlier?
simplified.plain_equation: In words: Models leftover emotional carryover from earlier events.
variables_explained: \omega_e is residue contribution from event e.
simplified.how_it_touches_agents: Residue is leftover feeling that does not vanish when the turn ends. It fades with a persistence factor and grows when new events leave a mark.
simplified.how_it_works: People do not reset after each event, some feeling remains and carries forward.
simplified.why_it_works: Carryover stops the agent from feeling freshly reset every message, which is what makes continuity feel real.
simplified.how_put_together: Residue can bias emotion selection and memory salience on later turns.
simplified.connects_to: Upstream inputs become numbers; downstream equations consume those numbers during the agent turn.

chapters.why_these_variables: α = each emotion depends on different state combinations; X = internal state drives displayed feeling.

chapters.simple_explanation: What should I remember for this moment?

simplified.how_it_works: Weighted linear score: simple, tunable, interpretable, debuggable. Favors relevant/recent/emotional memories; suppresses stale repetition.

chapters.why_these_variables: Min/max define the operating range for each channel.
chapters.simple_explanation: Put every signal on the same yardstick.

variables_explained: X_{\min},X_{\max} is observed or design bounds.

simplified.how_it_works: Without normalization, loud channels dominate soft ones for no psychological reason.
simplified.why_it_works: Shared scale is a prerequisite for fair blends and caps later.

simplified_intro.title: How the Continuity Model fits together
body: OtaconsKeep treats an agent as a persistent entity, not a blank prompt. Between turns the system keeps a numeric picture of how the agent feels, whom it trusts, what it remembers as important, and which traits are currently active.

The Continuity Model is a stack of small equations. Early equations turn dossier traits into weights and decide which traits matter in the moment. Mid-stack equations convert events into changes in mood and relationships, then pull those values back toward a baseline so nothing spirals forever. Later equations score memories, pick goals, resolve conflicts, and assemble the final reply.

Only a subset is wired into runtime code today (emotional state, blend and decay, comparison events, Formula 5 relationships). The rest is published design theory so the public evidence package matches the full model, not a marketing summary.
Simplified mode below walks each equation in plain language: what every symbol means, how it touches an agent during a Codec turn, why the form was chosen, and how the pieces connect.
